chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deposit of gold and silver. He said, 'Everything that is a deposit and is not guaranteed (liable for loss) is not liable (for compensation if lost).'
ai.seo_question: What is the liability of a custodian for deposited gold and silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the custodian of gold and silver is held to a strict liability standard (daman) unless explicitly agreed otherwise, reflecting the high value and ease of loss associated with precious metals. This ruling distinguishes wadi'ah (safekeeping) from qard (loan) and emphasizes the custodian's responsibility to safeguard these assets, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding commercial transactions.
